item.title: Medical Malpractice Defense Services
item.description:
NYC Health + Hospitals | Procurement | Solicitation | Due: 2026-11-02 In plain English (machine-written): NYC Health + Hospitals is seeking proposals from law firms to defend it and its medical staff in high-exposure medical malpractice claims, with responses due Nov. 2, 2026.

NYC Health + Hospitals seeks to obtain proposals from law firms that specialize in the defense of medical malpractice claims. The successfully awarded firms will defend NYC Health + Hospitals and its medical staff in high exposure medical malpractice claims.  Defense counsel may also be assigned to represent physicians insured by NYC Health + Hospitals' captive insurance company, the HHC Insurance Company (HHCIC) and its medical staff in regulatory matters.  Defense counsel is also expected to provide legal assistance concerning NYC Health + Hospitals Risk Management and Quality Assurance programs, be available to consult on regulatory matters, assist hospital risk managers and conduct in-service lectures.

item.title: Systemwide Commissioning Services
item.description:
NYC Health + Hospitals | Procurement | Solicitation | Due: 2026-10-16 In plain English (machine-written): NYC Health + Hospitals is seeking proposals from vendors for systemwide commissioning services, which verify that building systems at its facilities are installed and working as intended, with responses due Oct. 16, 2026.

NYC Health & Hospitals requests proposals for facility commissioning services related to new construction, facility renovations, re-commissioning of existing systems, or facility system assessments throughout its portfolio of buildings. The types of facilities to be commissioned may include office/administration, hospitals, health clinics, laboratories, or combinations thereof.

Commissioning is a systematic quality-assurance process used to verify and document that building systems and components are designed, installed, tested, started, operated, and maintained in accordance with NYC Health & Hospitals Project Requirements, Basis of Design, contract documents, and applicable performance criteria. The commissioning process shall confirm, prior to Substantial Completion and Owner acceptance, that the systems are complete and functioning as intended and that NYC Health & Hospitals facility staff have received adequate operating documentation and training…

item.title: Post Acute Care Debt Collection Services
item.description:
NYC Health + Hospitals | Procurement | Solicitation | Due: 2026-09-30 In plain English (machine-written): NYC Health + Hospitals is seeking proposals from debt collectors to recover unpaid patient balances at least 180 days old at its Post-Acute Care facilities, with responses due Sept. 30, 2026.

This Request for Proposal ('RFP') is issued in order to obtain debt collection services for facilities of NYC Health + Hospitals Post-Acute Care (PAC) for delinquent accounts with balances owned by the Patient. The accounts with balances owed by the patient or responsible parties are accounts with balances remaining unpaid at least 180 days after the first self-pay statement date.

The vendor will be responsible for the successful collection of funds owed for:

  • Private Pay accounts
  • Patient copays

item.title: Public Relations Services
item.description:
NYC Health + Hospitals | Procurement | Solicitation | Due: 2026-09-18 In plain English (machine-written): NYC Health + Hospitals is seeking proposals from public relations firms through a Request for Proposals, due Sept. 18, 2026, to support MetroPlusHealth's membership growth, reputation and media goals.

MetroPlusHealth is seeking a Public Relations vendor to support a strategic partnership to achieve the following outcomes:


Membership growth (Medicaid/Essential Plan/Medicare)
Reputation improvement targets
Share of voice vs competitors
Executive positioning goals (e.g., top-tier media placements per quarter)


The selected vendors objective will be to drive measurable growth in brand consideration, member acquisition, and reputation, with defined KPIs tied to earned media performance and
business outcomes.
